differences.text: Content is slotted (start, center, end) instead of ReactNode props. The roving items are the focusable leaves of the slotted content in flat-tree order, found through open shadow roots (a tct-button keeps its native button there); the focus target is the leaf itself, so tabindex is written on the inner control, never on a shadow host (a negative tabindex on a host removes its subtree from Tab).

The toolbar draws its own surface and dividers (upstream wraps a Section). The layout is always three columns (start | centre | end); an empty centre collapses, so the two-area and single-area layouts need no slot detection and are correct before JavaScript runs.

Edge compensation (ghost buttons and tabs sitting flush at the bar's edges) is done with ::slotted([data-tct-edge-comp]) on the first and last slotted child. It takes effect once ghost Button and tab elements set data-tct-edge-comp on their host (see requests).

A nested composite that runs its own roving tabindex (tct-segmented-control, tct-tab-list) keeps its own tab stop and arrows; the toolbar's arrows do not enter it. Upstream flattens every button, input and [tabindex] below the toolbar into one list; here two controllers writing tabindex on the same items would leave two tab stops.

The role, aria-label and aria-orientation are set through ElementInternals on the host; upstream ignores consumer role, aria-label and aria-orientation props, here a host aria-label attribute overrides the label property (an author who writes it means it).

requests.reason: Ghost buttons should reflect data-tct-edge-comp on the host so toolbars (and later banners and layout headers) can compensate their transparent padding at the edges, replacing upstream's data-astryx-edge-comp. No toolbar behaviour depends on it.

core.toolbar.notes: Guides: [mwg:accessibility] (toolbar as one composite tab stop, caret keys stay with text fields) [mwg:spatial-navigation] (arrow keys only inside the composite, focus target kept visible) [mwg:accessible-web-components] (role and aria-* through ElementInternals; no IDREFs across roots).
